record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: Can communication-efficient sub-model federated learning keep each client's sub-model choice private, characterize practical sparsity regimes, develop sparse secure aggregation for those regimes, co-optimize private information retrieval with secure aggregation, and preserve sparse updates under local or distributed differential privacy?

evidence.quote: keeping the client’s sub-model choice private

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a federated learning setting in which a central server coordinates training across N clients. The global model is partitioned into M disjoint sub-models (e.g., the rows of a large embedding table or the experts of a mixture-of-experts model). At each round, every client i selects a subset S_i ⊆ {1,...,M} of sub-models relevant to its local data, downloads the corresponding parameters, computes a sparse update supported on S_i, and contributes it to a server-side aggregate that updates only those coordinates. Address all of the following as a single design problem:

(1) Sub-model privacy. Design a protocol that allows each client i to download and update its chosen sub-models S_i without revealing S_i (or any non-trivial information about it) to the server or to other clients, even when the server is honest-but-curious and a bounded fraction of clients may collude.

(2) Sparsity regimes. Identify and rigorously characterize practical sparsity regimes — relations among the total number M of sub-models, the number N of clients, the per-client sparsity |S_i|, and the dimension d of each sub-model — under which communication- and computation-efficient private sub-model training is information-theoretically or computationally feasible.

(3) Sparse secure aggregation. Construct a secure aggregation protocol whose client and server communication and computation scale with the size of the union ⋃_i S_i (or with per-client sparsity |S_i|) rather than with M·d, while still ensuring that the server learns only the aggregate sum of client updates and nothing about individual updates or supports beyond what the aggregate reveals, in the sparsity regimes from (2).

(4) Joint PIR + secure aggregation. Co-design a private information retrieval mechanism for the download phase (clients retrieving the parameters of sub-models in S_i without revealing S_i) together with the sparse secure aggregation mechanism for the upload phase, optimizing the combined communication, computation, and round complexity rather than treating the two primitives independently.

(5) Differential privacy compatibility. Augment the protocol so that the output satisfies (ε, δ)-differential privacy under either the local model (each client perturbs its own update) or the distributed model (noise is generated jointly via secure aggregation), while preserving the sparsity of client updates — i.e., without forcing each client to transmit or noise a dense d·M-dimensional vector — and quantify the achievable privacy–utility–communication trade-offs.

Provide protocols achieving (1)–(5) simultaneously together with matching lower bounds, or prove impossibility results delineating the feasible parameter regimes.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works (e.g., PREAMBLE for block-sparse vector aggregation, LWE-based efficient DP secure aggregation, and protocols combining secure aggregation with multi-step local DP training) address individual sub-problems, but no protocol simultaneously achieves private sub-model selection, sparsity-proportional secure aggregation, jointly optimized PIR, and sparsity-preserving local/distributed differential privacy with matching tight trade-offs. The combined design problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Private and Efficient Aggregation of Block Sparse Vectors
status_evidence.snippet: PREAMBLE enables communication- and computation-efficient aggregation of block-sparse vectors, combinable with privacy amplification by sampling.
status_evidence.claim: Recent partial progress on sparse secure aggregation exists but does not cover private sub-model selection and joint PIR co-design.

status_evidence.title: Efficient Differentially Private Secure Aggregation for Federated Learning via LWE
status_evidence.snippet: Efficient DP secure aggregation based on hardness of LWE.
status_evidence.claim: DP-secure aggregation is studied but not jointly with private sub-model PIR or sparsity preservation.

status_evidence.title: On Using Secure Aggregation in Differentially Private FL with Multiple Local Steps
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work shows how parties can perform multiple local optimization steps while still benefiting from secure aggregation.
status_evidence.claim: Combining secure aggregation with DP under realistic communication constraints is an active and incomplete research area.
